title.narrative: Spotlight Initiative - Gender Transformative Joint Programme for the Promotion of Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment: Towards the Elimination of Gender Based Violence

description.narrative: Outcome C: Women and girls who experience violence and harmful practices benefit from available, accessible, acceptable, and quality essential services. The outcome will focus on ensuring that multi-sectoral service providers have the capacity to deliver inclusive, survivor-centred, high quality and coordinated services (including justice and accountability). This is with the assumption that services are supported by guidelines, protocols and policies developed through consultation with women’s rights organisations. And lastly, these services are made available and accessible to all survivors, women and girls and we expect women and girls who have experienced violence or are at risk will benefit from available, accessible, acceptable and quality essential services because we know barriers to services have been addressed and systems have been adapted to better meet the needs of women and girls. This outcome will focus on strengthening gender equality and GBV coordination platforms at national and sub-national levels. The coordination will be at no cost to the programme. Government leads on this Institutionalize coordination structures, referral mechanisms and case management services through SOPs and guidelines. This, in addition to training, will mitigate the risks posed by the frequent GRZ staff rotations, which lead to fragmented approaches to advancing GEWE and eliminating GBV as well as a lack of continuity and jeopardized institutional memory. This coordination the programme will just follow up and ensure meetings are taking place and minutes are kept in good order. Othe interventions will include analysing existing knowledge gaps, existing curriculums, adapt/design learning curriculums and roll out training on survivor-centred referrals and coordination processes to Government Service Providers (Police Officers, Customs Officers, Disaster Management Officers, Judicial officers, Judiciary, Social Welfare Officers, Community Development Officers, Health Practitioners, Prosecutors, Paralegals, Legal Aid Counsels, Immigration Officers and Extension Officers, Teachers and School Administrators) at OSCs, FTCs, and Police Stations. This, in addition to training, will mitigate the risks posed by the frequent GRZ staff rotations, which lead to fragmented approaches to advancing GEWE and eliminating GBV as well as a lack of continuity and jeopardized institutional memory. Further, the outcome will provide training for teachers, school counsellors, and education administrators on how to identify signs of school related GBV/GBV among students and how to make referrals to appropriate services. In line with the whole-of-school approach adopted by the programme, learners and teachers will be expected to establish a safe and confidential reporting mechanism to report incidents of Technology Facilitated GBV and train school staff on how to respond to TF GBV reports in a sensitive and supportive manner. Sensitization of learners about responsible online behaviour and how to protect their own privacy and themselves from online abuse will also be part of the programme. This will also include an orientation on peer-support and on the bystander intervention concept to support each other.
